paper_recipe_vs_adaptation: TP-YOLOv8 uses a modified small-object architecture and scratch training on TAT (not available here); do not claim reproduction. S12 publisher abstract compares n/s/m and favors s with 100 epochs; full tables were not accessible, so no numerical metric or optimizer is attributed to it. Ultralytics suggests increasing resolution and reducing heavy augmentation for small-object/limited-data plateaus. This project adapts these ideas using standard COCO-pretrained v8s, 960 pixels, mosaic .5 and scale .3. These are project hypotheses, not paper-proven optimal values.
experiment_purpose: Test a combined capacity/resolution/augmentation/horizon recipe after 21 of 37 validation misses had GT min side below 32px at 640. Same dataset bytes, source groups, validation and evaluation thresholds as normal-expanded v1. This is not a single-variable ablation; no individual change can receive causal credit.
hardware_decision: RTX3050Ti 4GB: batch2, FP32 and workers0 reduce activation/RAM pressure; nbs64 retains nominal gradient accumulation. Forward-only preflight cannot guarantee backward memory. Do not silently change batch/imgsz/AMP on OOM: preserve failure and create a new config.
limitations: Same 217-image validation has been used repeatedly; positive labels mark first-visible-impact only, not dense video events. 18 normal scene groups are provisional and camera independence is unproven. No promise of exceeding 70% mAP50 or F1; do not report it as accuracy, mAP50-95 or event performance. Old consumed test and sealed 120-frame negative holdout are not used for selection. More capacity/resolution increases runtime and may overfit. No additional dataset is required for this controlled pilot comparison.
